description: Advanced Navigation is a Sydney-based developer of Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) systems that provide users with highly accurate positioning data, even in environments where GPS signals are jammed, spoofed or unavailable. Founded in 2012, the company has since deployed over 100,000 systems to a global customer base.

Advemto has developed, and demonstrated, a breakthrough technology for improving the measurement of fluorescent markers used across life sciences. The company is applying this core IP to Smart Plates: a consumable that links immune cell behaviour to genetic identity at single-cell scale, without requiring customers to purchase any new hardware.

Alimetry has developed diagnostic technology for gastric dysfunction, aiming to provide an “EKG for the stomach.” Its first product is a non-invasive wearable device that uses 64 electrodes to measure stomach muscle activity, with results transmitted wirelessly for clinician analysis and visualisation.

Atomic.io is a low-code platform enabling enterprises to deliver highly personalised, interactive in-app messages securely and at scale. From nudging customers through key decisions to rewarding milestones and replacing costly SMS, the platform turns a company’s app into its most trusted and impactful communication channel.

Auror provides a crime intelligence system to brick-and-mortar retailers, used by front-line store employees, headquarters staff and the police to help prevent organised crime, reduce loss from theft and make stores feel safer for employees.

AutoGrab is an Australian based automotive intelligence platform that provides real-time data and insights to dealers, insurers, lenders, and fleet operators, by offering a suite of products including live pricing, vehicle sourcing, inventory management, pre-accident valuations and fleet management.

Avasa is a groundbreaking MedTech startup founded by surgeon-turned-bioengineer Dr. Nandoun Abeysekera, who developed a novel tubular tissue transformer to automate and standardise microvascular surgery procedures, specifically arterial anastomosis. This technology is poised to disrupt the current manual method, offering clinicians a precise, easy-to-adopt tool to improve patient clinical outcomes with minimal upskilling required.

B.Spkl is developing a novel method for producing high-performance, low-cost catalysts, initially targeting the hydrogen electrolyser market. By using a single-stage process to vastly simplify the catalyst manufacturing process, the company creates significant cost savings and enables a more cost-effective and scalable production of clean Hydrogen.

With increased EVs, solar, and home energy electrification seen across the world, Basis developed a new smart panel, designed to replace traditional residential switchboards with a digital system that gives homeowners real-time visibility and control over their energy usage, modernising how household electricity is managed, improving safety and efficiency, and allowing faster installation compared to conventional switchboards.

description: Cadmus Animal Health is a New Zealand-based company developing an immunotherapeutic for periodontal disease in companion animals. Rather than cleaning and extraction once damage is done, it trains the animal's immune system against the Porphyromonas bacteria that drive the disease. The company spun out of Denteric, a human health company built on University of Melbourne research into the same bacteria.

Crimson Education was founded in 2013 with a focus on university admissions, and quickly expanded into a broader platform supporting high-performing students across their education journey. At its core is technology that enables personalised, data-driven learning and support at scale, informed by a growing dataset and consistently strong outcomes.

Dawn Aerospace is creating next-generation space transportation with a focus on building eco-friendly satellite propulsion systems and reusable spaceplane technology. It has become the world's leading supplier of green in-space propulsion, with more than 200 thrusters flown across 50-plus satellites. Its Mk-II Aurora, a rocket-powered suborbital spaceplane, is the first privately developed aircraft to fly supersonic since Concorde and is now taking commercial orders.

Evnex produces AC (Alternating Current) electric vehicle chargers for homes and workplaces, paired with interoperable software that enables electricity distributors to dynamically manage when chargers draw power from the network. They currently facilitate the largest network of residential and workplace chargers in NZ and have relationships with more than ten electricity distributors including Vector and Powerco.

Fleet Space Technologies is an Australian company building the leading platform for mineral exploration. It pairs proprietary satellite and sensor technology with an AI model to produce 3D subsurface models in hours rather than months, improving outcomes and lowering environmental impact for miners. The technology also extends to defence and space.

Founded in 2017, Hnry is an all-in-one financial platform for sole traders, integrating payments, banking, accounting tools, and professional accountancy across New Zealand, Australia, and the United Kingdom. Beyond tax, it streamlines end-to-end financial administration across 300+ verticals through a fully integrated, automated solution.

description: Founded in 2010, Kindo began as a solution to a common parenting challenge: to make healthy school lunches easy for families and effortless for schools. Since then, it has evolved to become New Zealand's leading school payments platform, supporting lunches, payments and e-commerce for schools nationwide.

The Kry10 Operating System (KOS) and Platform is a new operating system and management service aimed directly at connected devices. Unlike alternatives, it is highly secure, providing ultimate protection from attack. Founded by Boyd Multerer, ex-Microsoft and the technical brains behind the Xbox live architecture, the platform is designed for industrial systems, infrastructure, transport, and government.

LawVu is an NZ mid-market SaaS company selling software servicing; matters, contracts, insights and other capabilities to in-house legal teams primarily in NZ, the UK and US. The cloud-based platform was looking to take advantage of the movement of corporate functions towards digital adoption, giving legal departments a clearer view of operations and providing a complete end-to-end system.

Every year, more than US$80 billion worth of valuable metals are lost to waste, with electronic and automotive waste accounting for around half of that total. Recognising both the challenge and opportunity, Mint Innovation developed the world's first biorefinery using their patented biometallurgical process to sustainably extract critical metals (such as gold, palladium and copper) from electronic waste and other feedstocks, helping build more resilient and circular supply chains for the materials our world increasingly depends on.

Miruku is developing a novel technique for producing alternative dairy proteins through a molecular farming platform. Their approach involves growing proteins directly in plants, where cells are recruited as mini-factories to produce proteins, fats, and sugars that are normally only sourced from animals. The four founding team members are considered to be among the best in the world in their fields, both scientifically and commercially.

Open is a digital insurance platform that provides the backend technology for brands to offer embedded insurance products to their customers. The company aims to make insurance simple, accessible and affordable for everyone.

description: ParkHelp (originally Parking Sense) offered parking guidance and curbside management technology. The company had expanded globally and developed its product portfolio as it positioned itself as a leader in digitising the global parking industry.

description: Portainer provides an operational toolset to simplify the use of container orchestration systems. Its products give enterprise IT and operational technology teams a single control plane to deploy, govern and update container workloads across multi-cluster, edge and air-gapped environments. The software has had remarkable engagement around the world, with over 2b pulls and 500k developers and IT engineers using it monthly (and growing).

PowerbyProxi first began as a spin-out from the University of Auckland’s Engineering School, built on nearly three decades of wireless power research, and successfully commercialised its technology across industrial and consumer applications. Heralded as a developer of the world’s most advanced and safest wireless power system, it was acquired by Apple in October 2017.

Built for owners, operators, and investors, Re-Leased streamlines property management with intelligent workflows that save time, reduce costs, and minimise risk, while providing a single source of truth across portfolios with instant visibility into performance, compliance, and operations.

RespirAq is a MedTech company developing a humidification system for hospital ventilators. Patients who rely on ventilators need humidified air to protect and maintain their airways, but typically systems depend on external water-based components and complex setups. RespirAq’s Active Humidifier removes the need for added water by using a smart membrane and integrated heating to manage moisture directly, improving reliability in critical care settings — an innovation that has since earned U.S. FDA Breakthrough Device Designation.

Born from the founders PhD’ research, RosterLab’s AI-driven engine is revolutionising hospital rostering. Its SaaS solution uses a proprietary algorithm to streamline staff scheduling, managing over 50 rules simultaneously (incl. union regulations, staff preferences, and skill sets), to reduce rostering time by up to 90%. By freeing senior physicians from admin and prioritising staff preferences, RosterLab enables its customers to unlock improved efficiency and staff retention, and reduce burnout.

Solve provides enterprises with a real-time data warehousing and management solution which can be hosted in the customer’s own cloud, acting as a single source of truth, reconciling all of the customer engagement and touchpoints as well as providing audit trails for all database changes.

Static Technologies is a New Zealand FinTech startup taking an offensive approach to fraud and scams. While conventional tools detect phishing and scam campaigns after the fact, Static intervenes while an attack is still running, disrupting criminal operations and generating actionable intelligence so organisations can stop losses before money moves. The platform focuses on the early stages of an attack, the window that carries most of the damage and the one traditional fraud and cyber tools tend to miss. It is purpose-built for the institutions fraudsters impersonate to gain legitimacy: banks, telcos and government agencies. Static works across New Zealand and Australia and is expanding into North America.

SupaHuman has developed an AI compliance and authoring platform for vocational education providers. It codifies each provider's way of working to generate audit-defensible assessment and moderation materials, keeps them compliant as standards change, and gives educators more time to focus on better learner outcomes.

Tectrax has developed an electronic amphibious system for the aluminium boat market. The company partners worked with NZ’s leading boat builders to fit amphibious systems to aluminium or fibre-glass hulls, allowing the company to leverage OEM sales channels, give boat owners access to amphibious technology without changing brands, and showcase NZ boat manufacturers in international markets.

Timely is a specialist provider of appointment management and point of sale systems targeted at the beauty industry. EverCommerce, a US-based service commerce platform, saw the opportunity to build out their Fitness and Wellness portfolio through a bolt-on acquisition of Timely in 2021.

Built on 20 years of experience delivering tracking, telemetry, and operational intelligence to mission-critical environments, TracPlus provides aerial firefighting teams with a real-time view of aircraft, drops, and operations. With a strong focus on safety, efficiency, and precision, it helps wildfire agencies coordinate faster and respond with confidence.

Founded in 1998, TradeMe was a pioneer of NZ’s online C2C marketplace and online customer acquisition and endures as a dominant local platform and player. It was sold to Fairfax Media in 2006 for $750 million.

Tradify was founded by then-tradie Curtis Bailey, who was frustrated by the paperwork involved in running a trade business. The platform simplifies essential workflows including quoting, invoicing, job tracking, and payments, making it easier to manage core business tasks and focus on the work itself. It was sold to the Access Group in 2024.

Unleashed provides manufacturing companies with tools that help them streamline operations and manage inventory. Founded in 2009, the company now has over 2,000 customers in key markets – NZ, AUS, the US and UK. In 2020, the company was acquired by Access Group, a leading provider of business management software to mid-sized UK companies.

Shortly after the first iPad came out, Vaughan Fergusson recognised the opportunity to leverage the hardware as a Point of Sale (POS) solution, thus launching cloud POS software company Vend. As a specialist provider of a cloud based retail system, Vend became well established globally with over 11,000 clients in 140 countries (as at 2016).

Wellumio is developing a revolutionary imaging technology that harnesses the power of nuclear magnetic resonance for communities that are least able to access MRI. The company's first product, Axana, is a portable brain scanning device that enables paramedics and first responders to rapidly identify and characterise stroke in patients. The Wellumio team brought deep domain expertise and prior startup experience, an ideal blend of skills befitting the company’s needs. Both founders had previously started companies in relevant industries and had worked together for a number of years prior.

description: ZeroJet is creating the world’s first turnkey electric jet propulsion unit for boats. Doing much more than electrifying marine propulsion, its fully enclosed electric jet propulsion system improves safety by eliminating exposed propellers, enhances usability through quieter operation, and delivers strong performance while reducing environmental impact.
